My ProctoAct Gantt Chart

Complete guide — Projects, Tasks, Timeline & WBS

🚀

Section 1 — Getting Started

Creating a Project
On the Gantt Dashboard, click New Project (the button in the header toolbar). Enter a project name and optional description, then click Save Project. The new project card appears on the dashboard immediately.
Opening a Project Gantt View
Click anywhere on a project card or click the Open Gantt → link at the bottom of the card. The full task table and timeline will load. Use the ← Dashboard button (top-left) to return to the project list.
Adding a Main Task
Inside a project, click + Add Task (top-right). Fill in: Task Name, PIC (Person In Charge), Status, Start Date, End Date, Work Days, Completion %, and optional Remarks. Click Save Task. The task appears in the WBS table and a bar appears on the timeline.
Adding a Sub-task
Click + Sub on any task row in the Actions column, or click + Add Sub-task at the top. A parent task selector appears — choose the parent task, then fill in the sub-task details. Sub-tasks are indented under their parent in the WBS and shown as thinner bars on the timeline.
📋

Section 2 — Task Fields Explained

WBS (Work Breakdown Structure)
Assigned automatically. Main tasks get numbers like 1, 2, 3. Sub-tasks get 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 etc. WBS is shown in the first column of the task table for easy reference.
Status Options
Not Started Task is planned but work hasn't begun.
In Progress Task is currently being worked on.
Delayed Task is behind schedule.
Completed Task is fully done.
Work Days & Include Weekends
Work Days is the number of working days for the task. ProctoAct auto-calculates it from Start and End dates (excluding weekends by default). Toggle Include Weekends if the task runs through Saturday/Sunday. Changing any one of Start Date, End Date, or Work Days automatically recalculates the others.
Completion %
Use the slider or type a number (0–100). The darker-filled portion of each bar on the timeline represents how much of the task is done. A task can be In Progress at 100% if it isn't formally marked Completed yet.
🗓

Section 3 — Reading the Gantt Timeline

Timeline Header Rows
The timeline header has three rows: Month (top, blue/indigo gradient), Week (middle, deep indigo), and Day (bottom, showing Mon–Sun dates). Weekend columns are lightly shaded.
Navigating Weeks
Use the ‹ and › arrow buttons in the toolbar to scroll the timeline one week at a time. Use the month/year dropdown to jump directly to a specific month. The timeline auto-scrolls to today when a project loads.
Today Marker
A vertical orange line marks today's date on the timeline. It also highlights today's date column header in orange. Use the timeline to see which tasks are on track, running late, or not yet started.
Clicking a Bar to Edit
Click any coloured bar on the timeline to open the Edit Task form for that task. The darker-filled portion shows completion. Hover over a bar to see its name and status in a tooltip. You can also edit tasks using the Edit button in the Actions column.
⚙️

Section 4 — Managing Projects

Editing a Project
On the dashboard, click Edit on a project card to update its name or description. All tasks remain unchanged.
Deleting a Project (Recycle Bin)
Click Del on a project card. The project moves to the 🗑️ Recycle Bin (top-right of the header) and is kept for 7 days. You can restore it at any time during this period. After 7 days it is permanently removed.
Collapse / Expand Sub-tasks
Click the ▾ chevron next to a parent task's WBS number to collapse its sub-tasks and hide them from the table and timeline. Use the Collapse All / Expand All buttons in the toolbar to toggle all at once.
Deleting a Task
Click Del in a task row's Actions column. You will be asked to confirm. Deleting a parent task will also remove all its sub-tasks. This action is permanent — the Recycle Bin only applies to whole projects.
Searching Projects
Use the 🔍 Search gantt timelines... bar in the header to filter project cards by name in real time. The search only applies to the dashboard — clear it to see all projects again.
📷

Export as PDF

Download Gantt Chart as PDF
Click the 📷 PDF button in the section header to generate a formatted PDF — includes a branded header with your name and timestamp, and all current data in a clean print-ready layout.

ProctoAct Gantt Chart · Version 1.45.5
📚

Knowledge Hub. Quick Start Guide.

Focus on what matters. We’ll handle the rest.

⚙

Section 1 — The Basics

Creating a Task
Click the + New Task button in the header (or press N). Fill in the mandatory fields: Title, Category, and Start & End Dates. Optionally set Urgency, Status, and whether to Assign to a Coworker before saving.
Task Categories
Project — A long-running goal or initiative.  Things to Do — Personal tasks and reminders.  Action Item — Something that needs immediate attention.
Status Definitions
⏱ Pending Not yet started — the task is queued.
⚡ In Progress Actively being worked on right now.
✓ Completed Done. Task moves out of active views.
Urgency Levels
Four levels: Low → Medium → High → Critical. Urgency is shown as a coloured badge on every card and can be used as a filter.
Sub-Tasks
Click ✚ Add on any Kanban card to break a task into smaller steps. Each sub-task has its own title, description, dates, and status. Progress is shown as a ring on the parent card.
Assigning to a Coworker
When creating or editing a task, toggle 👤 Assign to Coworker to mark the task as someone else’s responsibility. Enter the coworker’s name in the field that appears. If the toggle is off, the task is assigned to you. The assigned name (or Me) is shown on every Kanban card so you can see who is the PIC at a glance.
🗺

Section 2 — Dashboard Navigation

My ProctoAct Calendar (Gantt View)
A week-by-week Gantt grid showing how long each task spans across a Monday–Sunday calendar. Each task bar is colour-coded by category. Use the month & year selectors to navigate. Only Pending and In Progress tasks appear here.
My ProctoAct Roadmap
A horizontal scrolling deck of cards showing all your active Projects, To-Dos, and Actions. Cards are sorted by end date so the most urgent always appear first. Each card shows timeline fill, days remaining, and progress.
Kanban Board (3 Columns)
The main workspace. Three columns — Pending, In Progress, and Completed — show all your tasks as cards. Click any card to expand sub-tasks, or use the action buttons to edit, close, or move it to the Recycle Bin.
Recycle Bin
Deleted or closed tasks go here. Click the 🗑 Recycle Bin icon button in the header toolbar. You can restore tasks back to the board or permanently delete them.
⚡

Section 3 — Power-User Features

Drag & Drop (Roadmap)
Click and hold any Roadmap card, then drag it into the In Progress or Completed drop zone that appears at the bottom of the roadmap. Release to update the task status instantly — no editing required.
Filtering & Search
Use the search bar to find tasks by name. Use the Category and Urgency dropdowns to narrow results. All views — Kanban, Calendar, and Roadmap — sync together and show only the matching tasks.
Backup & Restore
Open ⋮ More Options and click Export to download your full task list as a .json file. Use Import to restore it on any device — useful as a manual backup.
Light & Dark Mode
Toggle between themes using the ☼ / ☾ switch in the header. Your preference is saved automatically and persists across sessions.
Keyboard Shortcuts
N New Task    F Focus Search    Esc Close any modal
Print & User Manual
Click the Download / Print PDF button in the footer of this guide to open the browser print dialog — choose Save as PDF to keep a copy, or send directly to a printer.
📊

Section 4 — Status Reporting & PDF Exports

Open the Full Summary Report
Click the 📊 Summary button directly in the header toolbar. A modal opens showing all tasks grouped by status — Overdue, In Progress, Pending, and Completed — each in its own colour-coded section with timeline, progress, urgency, and KPI markers.
Export a PDF Report
Inside the Summary Modal, click 🖶 Export PDF Report to generate a clean, print-ready PDF of that status list — including task title, category, timeline, progress %, and urgency badges. Useful for sharing with your team or keeping an offline record.
Smart Sorting & Indicators
Tasks inside the report are sorted chronologically by start date. ⭐ KPI badges, ∞ TBD open-end-date markers, and sub-task progress ratios are all carried over into the summary and the exported PDF automatically.
📝

Section 5 — ProctoAct Task Notes

Opening a Note
Every task card on the Kanban board (across Pending, In Progress, and Completed columns) displays a 📝 Add Note button in its action row. Clicking it opens a focused rich-text canvas bound exclusively to that task — without triggering the Task Detail view or any other modal. Once a note has been saved, the button highlights in sky-blue and reads 📝 Note so you can see at a glance which tasks have notes attached.
Rich-Text Formatting Toolbar
The editor provides a full inline toolbar with the following controls:

B Bold  •  I Italic  •  U Underline
Font Family — Inter, Arial, Georgia, Courier New, Times New Roman.
Font Size — Small (12 px), Medium (15 px), Large (20 px), XL (26 px).
• Bullet List — creates a standard unordered list inside the canvas.
✕ Clear — strips all formatting back to plain text.

All formatting is stored as HTML so it renders exactly as written on every re-open. Toolbar buttons reflect live active state while you type or select text.
Saving & Persistence
Click Save Note to commit your content. A ✓ Saved successfully indicator flashes briefly to confirm. Each note is stored in localStorage under the key proctoNotes_[taskId] — a dedicated, isolated namespace that is completely separate from the core task database (proctoact_v1). This keeps all Backup & Export operations lightweight, secure, and unaffected by note data.
Closing Without Saving
Click the × button, press Esc, or click outside the modal to close the editor without saving. Any unsaved changes are discarded; the previously saved note content remains intact in storage.
Data Safety & Backup Note
Notes are stored under their own proctoNotes_ keys and are not included in the JSON backup exported via Export Backup. This is intentional — it keeps backup files lean and focused on task structure. Clearing browser site data will erase notes alongside tasks; keep regular JSON exports as your primary recovery point.
🔗

Section 5 — Cross-section Integration

Linked CR — in the Task Form
When adding or editing a task inside a Gantt project, a Linked CR dropdown appears in the task form. Select an existing Change Request to formally link the task to a CR. This allows you to trace which change request drove a specific project task, giving you full auditability from CR approval to project delivery.
Add to Gantt — from a CR
In the CR Log, open any CR detail panel and click 📈 Add to Gantt. A dropdown lets you select the target Gantt project. The CR is then recorded as a linked change under that project, so the project timeline reflects the full scope of approved changes.
Dashboard Visibility
Gantt project and task statuses are reflected live in the Dashboard Command Center — the Gantt doughnut chart shows Not Started / In Progress / Delayed / Completed breakdowns, and the Roadmap surfaces any Gantt task with an end date falling within the selected 7/14/30-day window.

Official User Manual & Guideline
Version 1.45.5  |   |  Internal Use Only
⚠  Step 1 — Mandatory
INSTALLATION — Do This First

Make sure the very first thing you do is install the app by clicking the "⬇ Install App" button in the top-right header. This ensures full offline access and gives ProctoAct its own dedicated workspace — independent of your browser session. Once installed, the app is accessible from your desktop or taskbar and works without an internet connection.

1. Introduction

ProctoAct App is a self-contained, browser-based project and task management dashboard. It combines a Gantt-style calendar, a roadmap summary, and a Kanban board into a single Progressive Web App (PWA) that requires no server, no login, and works fully offline after installation. All data is stored locally in your browser.

2. Dashboard — KPI Tiles

The top row displays four real-time KPI tiles giving you an instant snapshot of your workload:

  • Pending — Tasks queued but not yet started.
  • In Progress — Tasks actively being worked on. These appear in the Calendar and Roadmap views.
  • Completed — Tasks marked Done. Archived from active views but retained for reporting.
  • Overdue — Tasks whose end date has passed without completion. Flagged with a red pulse animation across all views.

Clicking any tile filters the Kanban board to show only that status group.

3. My ProctoAct Calendar

A compact Gantt-style timeline that visualises all active Pending and In Progress tasks across a Monday-to-Sunday weekly grid. Each coloured bar represents one task, spanning from its Start Date to its End Date.

Reading the Grid
  • Each row is one week (Mon → Sun).
  • Bars spanning multiple weeks show a flat edge to indicate continuation.
  • The today column is highlighted with a blue top-border.
  • Hover a bar for a tooltip with status, urgency, category, and days remaining.
  • Click a bar to jump to that task on the Kanban board.
Month Navigation
  • Use ❮ / ❯ arrows to go to the previous or next month.
  • Use the Month / Year dropdowns to jump to any month directly.
  • Click "Today" to return to the current month. The nav bar glows blue when viewing the current month.
  • Click "Collapse" to hide the grid; click "Expand" to restore it.
Tip: Tasks are only visible in months they are scheduled in. Make sure all tasks have both a Start Date and an End Date for full Calendar visibility.
4. My ProctoAct Roadmap

A horizontally scrollable row of summary cards — one per active Pending or In Progress task. Unlike the Calendar, this section shows your full active pipeline regardless of selected month. Cards are sorted with overdue tasks first, then by nearest due date.

  • Large day number — Due date day. Overdue tasks pulse red.
  • Progress bar — How far through the task's scheduled window you are.
  • Days-left chip — Remaining days or overdue duration.
  • Click any card to jump to the matching Kanban task.
5. Task Management
Creating a New Task

Click "✚ New Task" (top-right header). Fill in Title, Description, Category, Urgency, Start Date, End Date, and Status, then click "Save Task". The task appears immediately across all views.

6. Task Categories

ProctoAct uses a three-tier category system:

CategoryColourIntended Use
Project Electric Blue Formal milestones, deliverables, or initiatives with a defined scope and timeline. Use for work contributing to a named project or workstream.
Things to Do Soft Amber General to-do items, administrative tasks, reminders, or recurring responsibilities that are not part of a formal project.
Action Item Emerald Green Specific actions from meetings or decisions requiring follow-up. Typically short-lived and outcome-focused — e.g. "Send report to stakeholder by Friday."
Urgency Levels
  • Low — Complete when capacity allows.
  • Medium — Standard priority; complete within the scheduled window.
  • High — Requires focused attention; do not delay.
  • Critical — Must be resolved immediately. Solid red badge in all views.
7. Data & PWA
  • 📥 Export — Download all tasks as a .json backup. Do this regularly.
  • 📤 Import — Restore from a backup. Warning: overwrites all existing tasks.
  • 📋 User Manual — Opens this document for print or "Save as PDF".
  • ⬇ Install App — Installs ProctoAct as a PWA for offline use with a dedicated app window.
Important: Clearing browser site data erases all tasks. Keep regular JSON exports as your recovery point.

ProctoAct Note. Quick Guide.

Your document hub for notes & meeting minutes.

📝

Section 1 - What is ProctoAct Note?

Overview
ProctoAct Note is a dedicated Document Management Hub — a fullscreen workspace separate from the main dashboard where you can create, organise, and manage rich-text Notes and Meeting Minutes linked directly to your active tasks. Unlike the inline per-task notes, ProctoAct Note gives you a persistent, scrollable document library that survives across sessions.
Accessing ProctoAct Note
Click the ☰ VIEWS tab pinned to the right edge of the screen at any time. A slide-in Workspace Switcher panel opens. Click 📝 My ProctoAct Note to enter the Document Hub. Click 💻 My ProctoAct App to return to the main dashboard. Press Esc to close the switcher.
📄

Section 2 - Creating & Managing Notes

Creating a New Note
Click 📝 Add New Note in the top-right header. A popup form opens where you configure the document before creating it:

• Document Type — Notes for general write-ups or Meeting Minutes for structured meeting records.
• Accent Color — 6 color tokens (Emerald, Sky Blue, Amber, Violet, Crimson, Teal) to visually distinguish cards.
• Subject — Link Task connects to an active In Progress or Pending task, or Custom for free-text subject.
• Sub-Subject / Description — e.g. "Meeting minutes with ABC Sdn Bhd".

Click Create Note → to add it to the library and open the editor instantly.
Dual-Pane Layout
The left sidebar lists all your active note cards sorted by newest first — each shows the accent color, type badge, sub-subject title, linked task or custom subject, and creation timestamp. Click any card to open it in the right workspace. Use the search bar to filter cards live by title, subject, or content.
Writing & Formatting
The editor provides a full rich-text toolbar: B Bold  •  I Italic  •  U Underline  •  text alignment  •  font family  •  font size (S / M / L / XL)  •  bullet lists  •  clear formatting.

You can also update document type, accent color, linked task, and sub-subject from the metadata panel above the toolbar at any time — all changes auto-save silently.
💾

Section 3 - Saving, Navigation & Recycle Bin

Saving & Navigating
Click 💾 Save in the toolbar to commit all changes and return to the note list. Click ← Back to return to the note list — any unsaved changes will be lost, so use 💾 Save first to keep your work. The ✓ Saved indicator in the header confirms each silent commit.
Recycle Bin & 7-Day Auto-Purge
Click 🗑 Delete in the toolbar to send the active note to the Recycle Bin. Open 🗑 Recycle Bin (top-right header) to see trashed items with deletion date and a days-remaining countdown.

• ↩ Restore — reinstates the note back to the active list.
• ✖ Delete — permanently removes immediately.
• Auto-Purge — on every app launch, notes deleted more than 7 days ago are automatically and permanently removed.
Data Persistence & Backup
All notes are stored under proctoSuiteGlobalNotesCollection — completely isolated from the task database. Notes are included in the JSON backup (Export Backup from the main app). When restoring a backup, a sky-blue badge confirms how many notes will also be restored alongside your tasks.
📚

Section 4 - Books: Grouping Your Notes

What is a Book?
A Book is a folder-like group that bundles related notes together in the sidebar — for example, a Book named "Process Flow Review" could hold separate notes for "Receiving Process", "Putaway Process", "Picking Process", and so on. Books keep long note lists organised without changing how individual notes are written or saved.
Creating a Book
Click 📚 New Book above the note list in the left sidebar. Give it a name and pick one of 6 accent colors, then click Create Book →. The Book appears as a collapsible section in the sidebar, ready to hold notes.
Moving a Note into a Book
You can assign or move a note to a Book in three places:

• On the card — every note card in the sidebar has a small 📚 book dropdown; pick a Book to move it in, or choose "— No Book —" to ungroup it.
• Inside the editor — open any note and use the Book field in the metadata panel to reassign it at any time; changes auto-save.
• At creation — when creating a note, pick a Book from the Book (optional group) field, or click the + button on a Book's header to open a new note that's pre-assigned to that Book straight away.
Managing Books
Click a Book's header to collapse or expand it — this state is remembered between visits. Use the ✎ rename icon to edit its name, or the 🗑 delete icon to remove the Book itself. Deleting a Book never deletes the notes inside it — they simply move back to the Ungrouped section at the bottom of the list. Notes that aren't assigned to any Book always appear under Ungrouped, and the search bar also matches against Book names.
🔗

Section 5 - Cross-section Integration

Add Note from an Issue
Open any Issue in the Issue Log detail panel and click 📝 Add Note. ProctoAct Note opens with the issue number and title pre-filled as the note subject, making it easy to capture investigation findings, workaround steps, or stakeholder comments tied directly to that issue.
Add Note from a CR
Open any Change Request in the CR Log detail panel and click 📝 Add Note. ProctoAct Note opens with the CR number and title pre-filled, perfect for recording approval decisions, implementation notes, or stakeholder sign-off details linked to that change.
Notes in Export & Backup
All notes are included in the JSON backup when you select Note in the Export Backup modal. Restoring a backup with a Note section will reload your full notes collection automatically.
📷

My ProctoAct CR Log
Change Request Tracking & Approvals
📋Section 1 - Overview
What is the CR Log?
The CR Log is a structured tracker for logging, reviewing, and approving project changes. Every CR is assigned a unique number (CR-001, CR-002…), optionally linked to a Gantt project, and tracked through a defined status workflow from Draft to Closed.
Accessing the CR Log
Open the VIEWS panel on the right edge and select CR Log. The header shows your greeting, a search bar, the + New CR button, and the Recycle Bin.
📊Section 2 - Dashboard Stats
Stat cards at a glance
Five cards at the top show: Total CRs, Open (Draft / Submitted / Under Review), Approved, Rejected, and Implemented. All counts update live as records change.
➕Section 3 - Creating a Change Request
Opening the New CR form
Click + New CR in the header. A form opens with all fields. The CR number (e.g. CR-001) is assigned automatically and cannot be edited manually.
Linking to a Gantt Project
Use the Link to Gantt Project dropdown to associate the CR with an existing project (optional). Once linked, the project name appears as a tag in the table row.
Required vs optional fields
CR Title, Status, and Priority are required. Description, Requestor, Date, Affected Scope, Justification, Impact, and Remarks are optional but build a complete audit trail.
▶Section 4 - Status Workflow
Standard lifecycle
DraftInitial idea, not yet formally submitted.
SubmittedFormally raised and awaiting assignment.
Under ReviewBeing evaluated by the team or approver.
ApprovedAccepted — ready to be implemented.
RejectedDeclined — document the reason in Remarks.
ImplementedChange successfully applied to the project.
ClosedRecord archived — no further action needed.
👁Section 5 - Viewing & Editing CRs
View detail
Click anywhere on a row — or the 👁 View button — to open the read-only detail panel showing all fields, status badge, priority, and linked project.
Edit a CR
Click ✎ Edit in the row or ✎ Edit CR inside the detail panel. Update any field and click Save CR to commit.
Delete a CR
Click 🗑 Delete on the row. The CR moves to the Recycle Bin (soft delete) for 7 days before permanent auto-removal. Restore it any time within that window.
🔍Section 6 - Filtering & Search
Search bar
Filters across CR number, title, requestor, and description in real time as you type.
Status & Priority filters
Use the All Statuses and All Priorities dropdowns to narrow the table. Filters stack — combine search text with status and priority simultaneously.
🗑Section 7 - Recycle Bin
Soft delete & recovery
Deleted CRs are held for 7 days. Click the 🗑 bin icon in the header to open it. Each entry shows a countdown timer. Click ↩ Restore to recover or 🗑 Delete to remove permanently.
Empty Bin
The 🔥 Empty Bin button permanently deletes all items at once. This cannot be undone — use with caution.
📷

My ProctoAct Issue Log
Bug & Issue Tracker
🔗Section 1 - Overview
What is the Issue Log?
The Issue Log is a structured tracker for logging, managing, and resolving bugs, defects, and operational issues. Every issue is assigned a unique number (ISS-001, ISS-002…), categorised by type and priority, and tracked through a defined status workflow from Open to Closed.
Accessing the Issue Log
Open the VIEWS panel on the right edge and select Issue Log. The header shows a search bar, the + New Issue button, and the Recycle Bin icon.
📊Section 2 - Dashboard Stats
Stat cards at a glance
Five cards at the top show: Total Issues, Open, In Progress, Resolved, and Closed. All counts update live as records change.
➕Section 3 - Creating an Issue
Opening the New Issue form
Click + New Issue in the header. A form opens with all fields. The issue number (e.g. ISS-001) is assigned automatically and cannot be edited manually.
Required vs optional fields
Issue Title, Status, Priority, and Owner are required. Description, Reporter, Date Logged, Affected Area, and Resolution/Remarks are optional but build a complete audit trail.
Issue categories
Choose from: Bug, Feature, Improvement, Task, or Question. Categories help filter and group issues for better visibility.
▶Section 4 - Status Workflow
Standard lifecycle
OpenNewly logged — acknowledged but not yet being worked on.
In ProgressActively being investigated or fixed by the owner.
ResolvedFix applied — awaiting verification or sign-off.
ClosedVerified and confirmed — no further action required.
Won't FixAcknowledged but intentionally not addressed — document the reason in Remarks.
👁Section 5 - Viewing & Editing Issues
View detail
Click anywhere on a row — or the 👁 View button — to open the read-only detail panel showing all fields, status badge, priority, and category.
Edit an issue
Click ✎ Edit in the row or ✎ Edit Issue inside the detail panel. Update any field and click Save Issue to commit.
Delete an issue
Click 🗑 Delete on the row. The issue moves to the Recycle Bin (soft delete) for 7 days before permanent auto-removal. Restore it any time within that window.
🔗Section 6 - Cross-section Actions
📄 Raise CR from an Issue
Inside any issue detail, click 📄 Raise CR to jump to the CR Log with a pre-filled Change Request linked to the current issue. This ensures traceability between issues and change requests.
📝 Add Note from an Issue
Click 📝 Add Note inside the detail panel to jump to My ProctoAct Note with the issue title and number pre-filled as a reference note.
📋 Linked Issue — in the CR Form
When creating or editing a CR, a Linked Issue dropdown appears in the form. Select an existing Issue to formally connect the CR to its originating issue. The linked issue number appears as a tag on the CR row in the table, making it easy to trace the origin of every change request.
📝 Add Note from a CR
Inside any CR detail panel, click 📝 Add Note to jump to My ProctoAct Note with the CR number and title pre-filled as a reference note. Useful for capturing decisions, stakeholder comments, or implementation notes tied to a specific change.
📈 Add to Gantt from a CR
Inside any CR detail panel, click 📈 Add to Gantt to link the CR to a Gantt project. A dropdown lets you select the target project, and the CR is then listed as a linked change under that project — enabling full traceability from change request to project delivery.
🔍Section 7 - Filtering & Search
Search bar
Filters across issue number, title, owner, and description in real time as you type.
Status, Priority & Category filters
Use the All Statuses, All Priorities, and All Categories dropdowns to narrow the table. Filters stack — combine all three with search text simultaneously.
🗑Section 8 - Recycle Bin
Soft delete & recovery
Deleted issues are held for 7 days. Click the 🗑 bin icon in the header to open it. Each entry shows a countdown timer. Click ↩ Restore to recover or 🗑 Delete to remove permanently.
Empty Bin
The 🔥 Empty Bin button permanently deletes all items at once. This cannot be undone — use with caution.

My ProctoAct Daily Task
Daily Planner & Task Scheduler
📅Section 1 — Overview
What is My ProctoAct Daily Task?
My ProctoAct Daily Task is a visual weekly planner that lets you schedule tasks across a 7-day calendar grid with hourly time slots. Every task appears as a colour-coded card on the day and time you specify, giving you a clear at-a-glance view of your week.
Accessing Daily Task
Open the VIEWS panel on the right edge and select Daily Task. The header shows the ProctoAct logo, a search bar, + New Task, Copy From, and Bin buttons.
🗓Section 2 — Weekly Calendar View
The Time Grid
The main area is a 7-column grid (Mon – Sun) with hourly rows from 12 AM to 11 PM. Each cell represents a one-hour slot. The grid scrolls vertically and opens at 7 AM by default so your working hours are immediately visible.
Week Navigation
Use the ‹ and › arrows in the header to move backward or forward by one week. The current week range is displayed between the arrows. Click Today to jump back to the current week.
Search
Type in the search bar to filter tasks across all weeks by title. Matching cards remain visible; non-matching cards are hidden in real time.
➕Section 3 — Creating a Task
New Task Modal
Click + New Task to open the creation form. Fill in the Title, select a Date, pick a Time * and End Time * (both required), choose a Priority, and optionally add notes. Click Save Task to add it to the grid.
Required Fields
Time and End Time are compulsory. If either is left blank when you try to save, the field is highlighted in red and saving is blocked until both are filled in.
Priority Colours
Each priority is colour-coded on the card: High (red), Medium (amber), Low (green), and None (grey).
🃏Section 4 — Task Cards
Card Layout
Each task card displays the title, the time range, and a left-border in the priority colour. Completed tasks show a strikethrough on the title.
Selecting a Card
Click any task card to select it. The selected card gets a cyan glow border and a floating action bar (Complete / Edit / Delete) appears near the card. Click elsewhere on the grid to deselect.
✅Section 5 — Complete, Edit & Delete
Complete
Click ✓ Complete in the action bar to toggle the task as done. The title gets a strikethrough and the card dims slightly. Click Complete again to mark it undone.
Edit
Click ✏ Edit to reopen the task form pre-filled with existing details. Change any field and click Save Task. Time and End Time remain required.
Delete
Click 🗑 Delete to move the task to the Recycle Bin. The card is removed from the grid immediately. Deleted tasks can be restored from the Bin within 7 days.
↕Section 6 — Resizing Tasks
Drag to Resize
Hover over the bottom edge of a task card — the cursor changes to a resize handle. Drag downward to extend the End Time or upward to shorten it. Time snaps to the nearest 30-minute interval. The card updates live as you drag and saves automatically on release.
📤Section 7 — Send to Daily Task
Sending Items from Other Sections
Every item in My ProctoAct App, Gantt Chart, CR Log, and Issue Log has a 📅 Send to Daily Task button. Click it to open a scheduling modal for that specific item.
Scheduling Modal
The modal pre-fills the item title. Select the Date *, Time *, and End Time * (all required), optionally set a Priority and add notes. Click Add to Daily Task to place it on the calendar.
Recurrence Option
Toggle Recurring Task in the modal to schedule the item on a repeating basis. Choose Weekly (select specific days) or Monthly (select specific dates), and set a date range. The task is automatically placed on every matching occurrence.
⇅Section 8 — Copy From Modules
How Copy From Works
Click ⇅ Copy From in the Daily Task header to open a list of items from App, Gantt, CR Log, and Issue Log. Select the item you want, then set its Date, Time, and End Time (required) in the scheduling prompt that follows.
Source Tags
Each item in the Copy From list shows a source tag (TASK, GANTT, CR, ISSUE) so you can quickly identify where it came from before importing it.
🔁Section 9 — Recurring Tasks
Setting Up Recurrence
In the New Task or Send to Daily Task modal, toggle Recurring Task to reveal recurrence options. Choose Weekly to pick which days of the week (Mon–Sun) the task repeats, or Monthly to choose which dates each month.
Date Range
Set a Start Date and End Date for the recurrence. The system generates individual task instances for every matching day within that range, each appearing on the correct date column in the weekly grid.
Recurring Task Indicator
Recurring task cards display a 🔁 icon to distinguish them from one-off tasks at a glance.
🗑Section 10 — Recycle Bin
Accessing the Bin
Click the Bin button in the Daily Task header to view all recently deleted tasks. A red badge on the button shows the count of items currently in the bin.
Restoring Tasks
Each item in the Bin has a Restore button. Click it to return the task to its original date and time slot on the weekly grid. Tasks are automatically purged from the Bin after 7 days.

⚙️ General Guide
🔒 Security PIN
Setting up your PIN
On first launch, you are prompted to create a 4 or 6-digit PIN. Choose a PIN length, enter it twice to confirm, then select a security question and provide an answer. This answer is used to recover access if you forget your PIN.
Unlocking the app
Each time you open ProctoAct in a new browser session, you will see the PIN entry screen. Enter your PIN — the app auto-submits once the correct length is reached. The unlock persists for the entire browser session so you won't be asked again on page refresh.
Forgot PIN?
On the unlock screen, tap Forgot PIN? → answer your security question → set a new PIN. You can also update your security question at this step.
Changing your PIN & auto-lock
Go to More Options → Change Security PIN. Enter your current PIN to verify, then set a new PIN and optionally a new security question. You can also configure an Auto-Lock timeout (5 / 15 / 30 min / 1 hour) — the app will lock itself after that period of inactivity.
Lock Now
Open the Workspace Switcher (VIEWS tab on the right edge) and click the 🔒 Lock button in the panel header to instantly lock the app and return to the PIN screen — useful when stepping away from your device.
🗂️ Workspace Switcher
Opening the workspace panel
Click the VIEWS tab on the right edge of the screen (or tap the handle icon) to open the workspace panel. It shows your profile, stats, and quick links to all four workspaces.
Switching between workspaces
Use the navigation buttons inside the panel to switch between: App (tasks & projects), Note (document hub), Flow Chart (process maps), and Gantt Chart (project timelines). A ✓ indicator shows the active workspace.
Daily streak & stats
The panel shows your current task counts (active, notes, projects) and a daily usage streak. The streak increments each day you open and use ProctoAct.
👤 Profile & Settings
Rename profile
Tap More Options → Rename Profile, or click your name in the workspace panel to edit it inline. Your name is stored locally and shown in greetings and reports.
Avatar
Click your avatar in the workspace panel to choose from the built-in avatar library. Your selection is saved locally.
Dark / Light theme
Toggle between dark and light mode via More Options → Switch Theme. Your preference is saved and restored on next visit.
Export & Import backup
Export Backup downloads all your tasks as a JSON file — keep this as a safety copy. Import Backup restores tasks from a previously exported file. All data is stored in your browser's localStorage — clearing browser data will erase it, so export regularly.
⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts
Ctrl+K
Open command palette
N
New task (App view)
F
Focus search bar
Esc
Close any modal
Ctrl+S
Save active note
Ctrl+S
Save flow chart
🔐 Data & Privacy
All ProctoAct data — tasks, notes, flow charts, Gantt projects, your name, avatar, and PIN — is stored entirely in your browser's localStorage. Nothing is sent to any server. This means your data is private, works offline, but is tied to this browser. Use Export Backup regularly to avoid data loss.
📊 My ProctoAct Dashboard
Section 1 — What is the Dashboard?
The Dashboard is your Command Center — a single live screen showing real-time status across all four core sections: App, Gantt Chart, CR Log, and Issue Log. It opens automatically the moment you click Start, with no delay. All data is read directly from your local storage on every visit.
Section 2 — Command Overview (KPI Ribbon)
An Overall Completion ring sits above the ribbon, combining every done item across the App, Gantt, CR Log, and Issue Log into a single at-a-glance percentage. Below it, five large-number KPI cards run across the top of the screen:
• Active Tasks — pending + in-progress tasks from the App
• Critical Issues — open issues with High or Critical priority (turns red when > 0)
• Pending Approvals — CRs currently Submitted or Under Review
• In Progress Projects — Gantt projects currently in progress
• Overdue — tasks whose end date has passed and are not yet done (turns amber when > 0)

Click any KPI card to jump straight to that section. Hover for a tooltip explaining exactly what it counts — on touch devices, tap the small "i" button in the corner instead. When a number has changed since the last time you opened the Dashboard on a different day, a small ▲/▼ delta appears next to it.
Section 3 — Section Status Doughnut Charts
Each of the four sections is represented by an animated SVG ring chart that shows the status breakdown at a glance:
• App (green) — Pending / In Progress / Done / Overdue
• Gantt Chart (blue) — Not Started / In Progress / Delayed / Completed
• CR Log (purple) — Draft / Submitted / Under Review / Approved / Rejected / Implemented
• Issue Log (amber) — Open / In Progress / Resolved / Closed / Won't Fix

Each card also shows the exact count per status alongside the chart. Click View › on any card to jump directly to that section.
Section 4 — Roadmap
A scrollable list of all tasks and Gantt project sub-tasks with an end date falling within the selected window (including any already overdue). Use the 7d / 14d / 30d toggle in the header to widen or narrow the range — your choice is remembered. Each row shows:
• A colour-coded TASK or GANTT badge
• The item title
• A due-date label: Overdue Xd (red), Today (amber), Tomorrow / In Xd (blue/grey)

Click any roadmap row to jump straight to that specific task, project, or record. If nothing is due, the panel shows a clear-horizon message.
Section 5 — Needs Attention Feed
A prioritised action feed on the right column that automatically surfaces the most urgent items across all sections:
• Overdue tasks (highest urgency) — tasks past their deadline, shown with days overdue
• Critical / High issues — open issues that need immediate attention
• CRs Under Review — change requests awaiting a decision

The header shows a red item count. Click any row to navigate directly to that section. When everything is clear, the feed shows a “Nothing needs attention” confirmation.
Section 6 — Quick Add
The gradient ＋ Quick Add button in the top-right header opens a small dropdown menu with three shortcuts:
• New Task — switches to the App and opens the add-task form
• New CR — switches to CR Log and opens the new CR form
• New Issue — switches to Issue Log and opens the new issue form

This lets you log new items from the Dashboard without manually navigating away. Click anywhere outside the menu to dismiss it.
Section 7 — Live Sync & Refresh
The header displays a pulsing green LIVE indicator alongside the last-updated timestamp. All data is re-read every time you open the Dashboard. To force an instant re-read without navigating away, click the ↻ Refresh button — the timestamp updates to confirm the sync. The ✕ button in the header returns you to the App section.

My ProctoAct Flow Chart. Quick Guide.

Map your processes, SOPs, and workflows visually.

▦

Section 1 - What is My ProctoAct Flow Chart?

Overview
A dedicated Visual Workflow Mapping workspace — a fullscreen canvas to create and manage professional flowcharts across multiple named projects, each saved independently in your browser.
Accessing It
Click the ☰ VIEWS tab on the right edge of the screen. In the Workspace Switcher, click ▦ My ProctoAct Flow Chart. Press Esc to close the switcher.
📁

Section 2 - Projects

Creating a Project
Click + New Project in the left sidebar. Enter a name (e.g. "Onboarding Flow") and click Create Project →. Projects appear in the left sidebar — click any to switch to it.
Dual-Pane Layout
The left sidebar lists all your projects with node and arrow counts. Hover a card to reveal ✎ Rename and 🗑 Delete buttons. The right area is your active drawing canvas with a dot-grid background.
▦

Section 3 - Node Shapes

9 Standard Shapes
• ⬤ Start/End — Oval. Marks the start or end of the process.
• ▮ Process — Rectangle. A specific action or task to be performed.
• ◆ Decision — Diamond. A question or condition to be evaluated.
• ◯ Connector — Circle. Connects separate parts of the diagram.
• ∕ I/O — Parallelogram. Data entering or leaving the system.
• 📄 Document — Wavy bottom. Refers to an external document or file.
• 📑 Multi-doc — Stacked. Indicates several printed documents or reports.
• ⬟ Prep — Hexagon. Marks an adjustment or preparation step.
• 🗐 Text — Free label. Floating annotations anywhere on the canvas.
→

Section 4 - Connecting Nodes with Arrows

2-Click Connect
1. Click a node to select it — a glowing → button appears on its right.
2. Click → — all other nodes glow blue as valid targets.
3. Click any other node — arrow is drawn instantly.
Press Esc to cancel at any time.
Select & Delete Arrows
Click any arrow to select it (turns amber) — a red 🗑 button appears at its midpoint. Click it or press Del to delete. Double-click an arrow to add or edit a label.
⚙

Section 5 - Moving, Selecting & Saving

Moving & Renaming Nodes
Move: drag a node — all connected arrows re-route automatically. Rename: double-click any node, type the new label, press Enter. Delete: select a node then press Del or click the red ✕ button.
Multi-Select & Group Move
Drag on the empty canvas background to draw a lasso rectangle — all nodes inside are selected. Drag any selected node to move the whole group. Press Del to delete all selected nodes at once.
Saving
Click 💾 Save in the toolbar or press Ctrl+S / ⌘+S. All projects are stored locally in your browser — clearing site data will erase them, so save regularly.
🔗

Section 6 - Cross-section Integration

Raise CR from the Flow Chart
Click 📄 Raise CR in the Flow Chart header to jump directly to the CR Log with a new Change Request pre-filled and linked to your current Flow Chart project. Use this when a process diagram review identifies a change that needs to be formally tracked — keeping your visual workflows connected to your change management trail.
Export & Backup
Flow Chart data is included in the JSON backup when you select Flow Chart in the Export Backup modal. Restoring a backup with a Flow Chart section will reload your saved diagrams and project list automatically.
